    Coagulation Basic 3: PMF vs PDF (Builder + Coagulation)¶

    This notebook compares Brownian coagulation for PMF (discrete) and PDF (continuous) representations using the public builder pattern:

    • distribution_type="discrete" → PMF
    • distribution_type="continuous_pdf" → PDF

    Both are wrapped in par.dynamics.Coagulation. We run them over a short horizon for quick execution (<120 s). We also show how to convert between PMF and PDF using par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf for like-for-like comparisons.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    # In Colab uncomment the following command to install particula:
# Use the selected E9 checkout: `python -m pip install -e ".[extra]"`
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import particula as par
from scipy.integrate import trapezoid
    # In Colab uncomment the following command to install particula: # Use the selected E9 checkout: `python -m pip install -e ".[extra]"` import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import particula as par from scipy.integrate import trapezoid

    Build aerosols (PMF and PDF)¶

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    # Shared grid (modest resolution)
radius_bins = np.logspace(-8, -6, 140)  # m

# Lognormal parameters (kept small for speed)
mode = np.array([120e-9])
gsd = np.array([1.5])
number_conc = np.array([8e8])  # m^-3 total

# PMF (number per bin)
concentration_pmf = par.particles.get_lognormal_pmf_distribution(
    x_values=radius_bins,
    mode=mode,
    geometric_standard_deviation=gsd,
    number_of_particles=number_conc,
)

# PDF (number per size)
concentration_pdf = par.particles.get_lognormal_pdf_distribution(
    x_values=radius_bins,
    mode=mode,
    geometric_standard_deviation=gsd,
    number_of_particles=number_conc,
)

# Native ambient environment. GasData requires a species axis, so a
# zero-concentration, non-partitioning carrier fills that axis. Coagulation
# does not consume it; ambient pressure is specified independently.
environment = par.gas.EnvironmentData(
    temperature=np.array([298.15]),
    pressure=np.array([101325.0]),
    saturation_ratio=np.zeros((1, 1)),
)
gas = par.gas.GasData(
    name=["carrier"],
    molar_mass=np.array([0.02897]),
    partitioning=np.array([False]),
    concentration=np.zeros((1, 1)),
)

# PMF particles
particles_pmf = par.particles.create_particle_data_from_radii(
    radii=radius_bins,
    concentration=concentration_pmf,
    distribution_type="discrete",
    density=1000.0,
)

aerosol_pmf = par.Aerosol(
    particles=particles_pmf, gas=gas.copy(), environment=environment.copy()
)

# PDF particles
particles_pdf = par.particles.create_particle_data_from_radii(
    radii=radius_bins,
    concentration=concentration_pdf,
    distribution_type="continuous_pdf",
    density=1000.0,
)

aerosol_pdf = par.Aerosol(
    particles=particles_pdf, gas=gas.copy(), environment=environment.copy()
)
    # Shared grid (modest resolution) radius_bins = np.logspace(-8, -6, 140) # m # Lognormal parameters (kept small for speed) mode = np.array([120e-9]) gsd = np.array([1.5]) number_conc = np.array([8e8]) # m^-3 total # PMF (number per bin) concentration_pmf = par.particles.get_lognormal_pmf_distribution( x_values=radius_bins, mode=mode, geometric_standard_deviation=gsd, number_of_particles=number_conc, ) # PDF (number per size) concentration_pdf = par.particles.get_lognormal_pdf_distribution( x_values=radius_bins, mode=mode, geometric_standard_deviation=gsd, number_of_particles=number_conc, ) # Native ambient environment. GasData requires a species axis, so a # zero-concentration, non-partitioning carrier fills that axis. Coagulation # does not consume it; ambient pressure is specified independently. environment = par.gas.EnvironmentData( temperature=np.array([298.15]), pressure=np.array([101325.0]), saturation_ratio=np.zeros((1, 1)), ) gas = par.gas.GasData( name=["carrier"], molar_mass=np.array([0.02897]), partitioning=np.array([False]), concentration=np.zeros((1, 1)), ) # PMF particles particles_pmf = par.particles.create_particle_data_from_radii( radii=radius_bins, concentration=concentration_pmf, distribution_type="discrete", density=1000.0, ) aerosol_pmf = par.Aerosol( particles=particles_pmf, gas=gas.copy(), environment=environment.copy() ) # PDF particles particles_pdf = par.particles.create_particle_data_from_radii( radii=radius_bins, concentration=concentration_pdf, distribution_type="continuous_pdf", density=1000.0, ) aerosol_pdf = par.Aerosol( particles=particles_pdf, gas=gas.copy(), environment=environment.copy() )

    Configure coagulation runnables¶

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    coagulation_pmf = par.dynamics.Coagulation(
    coagulation_strategy=(
        par.dynamics.BrownianCoagulationBuilder()
        .set_distribution_type("discrete")
        .build()
    )
)

coagulation_pdf = par.dynamics.Coagulation(
    coagulation_strategy=(
        par.dynamics.BrownianCoagulationBuilder()
        .set_distribution_type("continuous_pdf")
        .build()
    )
)

print(coagulation_pmf)
print(coagulation_pdf)
    coagulation_pmf = par.dynamics.Coagulation( coagulation_strategy=( par.dynamics.BrownianCoagulationBuilder() .set_distribution_type("discrete") .build() ) ) coagulation_pdf = par.dynamics.Coagulation( coagulation_strategy=( par.dynamics.BrownianCoagulationBuilder() .set_distribution_type("continuous_pdf") .build() ) ) print(coagulation_pmf) print(coagulation_pdf)

    Execute short coagulation steps¶

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    time_step = 200  # seconds
sub_steps = 10

# PMF run
pmf_before = aerosol_pmf.particles.concentration[0].copy()
aerosol_pmf_after = coagulation_pmf.execute(
    aerosol_pmf, time_step=time_step, sub_steps=sub_steps
)
pmf_after = aerosol_pmf_after.particles.concentration[0].copy()

# PDF run
pdf_before = aerosol_pdf.particles.concentration[0].copy()
aerosol_pdf_after = coagulation_pdf.execute(
    aerosol_pdf, time_step=time_step, sub_steps=sub_steps
)
pdf_after = aerosol_pdf_after.particles.concentration[0].copy()
    time_step = 200 # seconds sub_steps = 10 # PMF run pmf_before = aerosol_pmf.particles.concentration[0].copy() aerosol_pmf_after = coagulation_pmf.execute( aerosol_pmf, time_step=time_step, sub_steps=sub_steps ) pmf_after = aerosol_pmf_after.particles.concentration[0].copy() # PDF run pdf_before = aerosol_pdf.particles.concentration[0].copy() aerosol_pdf_after = coagulation_pdf.execute( aerosol_pdf, time_step=time_step, sub_steps=sub_steps ) pdf_after = aerosol_pdf_after.particles.concentration[0].copy()

    Convert for apples-to-apples comparison¶

    We convert PDF⇄PMF using par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf so both representations can be compared on the same units.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    pdf_as_pmf_before = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf(
    x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pdf_before, to_pdf=False
)
pdf_as_pmf_after = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf(
    x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pdf_after, to_pdf=False
)

pmf_as_pdf_before = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf(
    x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pmf_before, to_pdf=True
)
pmf_as_pdf_after = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf(
    x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pmf_after, to_pdf=True
)

# Quick consistency check
number_pmf = pmf_before.sum()
number_pdf = trapezoid(pdf_before, x=radius_bins)
print(f"Total number PMF: {number_pmf:.2e} m^-3")
print(f"Total number PDF: {number_pdf:.2e} m^-3 (integrated)")
    pdf_as_pmf_before = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf( x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pdf_before, to_pdf=False ) pdf_as_pmf_after = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf( x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pdf_after, to_pdf=False ) pmf_as_pdf_before = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf( x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pmf_before, to_pdf=True ) pmf_as_pdf_after = par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf( x_array=radius_bins, distribution=pmf_after, to_pdf=True ) # Quick consistency check number_pmf = pmf_before.sum() number_pdf = trapezoid(pdf_before, x=radius_bins) print(f"Total number PMF: {number_pmf:.2e} m^-3") print(f"Total number PDF: {number_pdf:.2e} m^-3 (integrated)")

    Summary¶

    • PMF: distribution_type="discrete" via BrownianCoagulationBuilder
    • PDF: distribution_type="continuous_pdf"
    • Both run through par.dynamics.Coagulation
    • Conversions use par.particles.get_pdf_distribution_in_pmf for consistent comparisons across representations.
    • Runtime kept short with modest grids and a single 200 s step.

    Native construction uses the explicitly generated distribution above. The old preset construction regenerated default modal inputs instead. Finite-grid coagulation has numerical mass drift; these curves illustrate number loss, not exact conservation or a time-step/grid-convergence claim.
